title: Erdős #33: Additive Complements of Squares
description: For sets A such that every integer is n² + a for some a ∈ A, what is the minimum possible density? Best known: liminf ≥ 4/π ≈ 1.273 and limsup ≤ 2φ^(5/2) ≈ 6.66.

overview.historicalContext:
This problem concerns 'additive complements of squares' - sets A ⊆ ℕ such that every natural number can be written as n² + a for some a ∈ A. Erdős asked: how sparse can such a set be?

Moser (1965) proved the first quantitative lower bound: liminf |A ∩ {1,...,N}|/√N > 1.06. This was improved by Cilleruelo (1993), Habsieger (1995), and Balasubramanian-Ramana (2001) to the current best bound of 4/π ≈ 1.273.

For upper bounds, Van Doorn constructed a set achieving limsup ≤ 2φ^(5/2) ≈ 6.66 where φ is the golden ratio. The exact minimum of the limsup remains open.
overview.problemStatement:
Let A ⊆ ℕ be such that every integer can be written as n² + a for some a ∈ A and n ≥ 0. What is the smallest possible value of limsup |A ∩ {1,...,N}|/√N? Is liminf |A ∩ {1,...,N}|/√N > 1?

**Status**: Partially solved. Best bounds: liminf ≥ 4/π ≈ 1.273, limsup ≤ 2φ^(5/2) ≈ 6.66. Exact minimum OPEN.
overview.text: For sets A such that every integer is n² + a for some a ∈ A, what is the minimum possible density? Best known: liminf ≥ 4/π ≈ 1.273 and limsup ≤ 2φ^(5/2) ≈ 6.66.
overview.proofStrategy:
The formalization defines additive complements of squares and the normalized density function |A ∩ {1,...,N}|/√N. A single axiom is used:

1. **Best known lower bound** (axiomatized): liminf ≥ 4/π (Cilleruelo–1993, Habsieger–1995, Balasubramanian-Ramana–2001)

Moser's earlier 1.06 lower bound and Van Doorn's limsup construction are described in docstrings as historical and expository context but are not separately axiomatized in this formalization. We also prove the golden ratio satisfies φ² = φ + 1 and derive that liminf > 1 from the 4/π bound.
keyInsights: **Additive complement**: A set A 'completes' the squares if every integer is a square plus something from A
**Why √N normalization?**: Squares grow like n², so up to N there are ~√N squares. A complementing set needs ~√N elements per interval
**The 4/π bound**: Arises from Fourier analysis and Jacobi theta functions - the distribution of quadratic residues modulo n
**Golden ratio appearance**: Van Doorn's construction uses Fibonacci-like patterns, naturally involving φ = (1+√5)/2
**Gap remains**: Between 4/π ≈ 1.27 (lower) and 2φ^(5/2) ≈ 6.66 (upper) - the exact minimum is unknown

sections.title: Problem Statement and Background
sections.summary: States Erdős Problem #33 on additive complements of squares (partially solved): for a set $A$ such that every large integer is $n^2+a$ for some $a \in A$, what is the smallest $\limsup |A\cap\{1,\dots,N\}|/\sqrt N$, and is the $\liminf$ ratio strictly above 1? Bounds tightened from Moser (1965) through Cilleruelo/Habsieger/Balasubramanian-Ramana and Van Doorn.
sections.mathContext: Current bounds sandwich the liminf ratio at $\ge 4/\pi \approx 1.273$ and the limsup at $\le 2\varphi^{5/2} \approx 6.66$ (golden ratio $\varphi$); the exact minimal limsup value remains open.

sections.title: Core Definitions
sections.summary: Defines additive complements of squares, counting function, and normalized density

sections.title: Existence Results
sections.summary: Erdős: such sets exist with finite limsup > 1

sections.title: Lower Bounds on liminf
sections.summary: Historical: Moser's 1.06 lower bound (docstring at lines 68–72, not axiomatized). Axiomatized: cilleruelo_habsieger_lower_bound — liminf ≥ 4/π (lines 80–82). Proved: four_over_pi_approx showing 4/π > 1.27 (lines 85–90).

sections.title: Golden Ratio and Van Doorn
sections.summary: Defines goldenRatio = (1 + √5)/2 (line 95). Proves goldenRatio_squared: φ² = φ + 1 (lines 98–102). Defines vanDoornConstant = 2φ^(5/2) (line 105). Van Doorn's limsup ≤ 2φ^(5/2) construction is described in a docstring (lines 107–113) but is not axiomatized.

sections.title: Open Questions
sections.summary: Exact minimum of limsup, whether liminf can equal 1

conclusion.summary: We formalize Erdős Problem #33 on additive complements of squares - sets A where every integer is n² + a for some a ∈ A. The formalization includes the Moser and Cilleruelo-Habsieger lower bounds on liminf, Van Doorn's upper bound on limsup, and proves the golden ratio identity used in the construction.
conclusion.implications: This problem connects additive number theory with the distribution of quadratic residues. The appearance of 4/π suggests deep connections to harmonic analysis, while the golden ratio bound hints at optimal greedy algorithms and Fibonacci-like structures.
openQuestions: What is the exact minimum value of limsup |A ∩ {1,...,N}|/√N?
Can the 4/π lower bound on liminf be improved?
Is there a connection between the optimal liminf and limsup for a single set A?

mainTheorems.name: IsAdditiveComplementOfSquares
mainTheorems.description: Defines a set A ⊆ ℕ as an additive complement of the squares when every natural number can be written as a + n² for some a ∈ A and n ≥ 0.

mainTheorems.name: countingFunction
mainTheorems.description: The counting function giving the number of elements of A in the interval {1, ..., N}.

mainTheorems.name: normalizedDensity
mainTheorems.description: The normalized density |A ∩ {1,...,N}| / √N whose limsup and liminf govern Problem 33.

mainTheorems.name: cilleruelo_habsieger_lower_bound
mainTheorems.description: The best known lower bound (Cilleruelo, Habsieger, Balasubramanian-Ramana) asserting liminf of the normalized density is at least 4/π for any additive complement of squares.
mainTheorems.leanType:
(A : Set ℕ)
    (hA : IsAdditiveComplementOfSquares A) :
  (4 / π : ℝ) ≤ liminf (fun N => normalizedDensity A N) atTop

mainTheorems.name: four_over_pi_approx
mainTheorems.description: Establishes that the lower-bound constant 4/π exceeds 1.27, using Mathlib's bound π < 3.15.

mainTheorems.name: goldenRatio
mainTheorems.description: The golden ratio φ = (1 + √5) / 2, which appears in Van Doorn's upper-bound constant.

mainTheorems.name: goldenRatio_squared
mainTheorems.description: Proves the defining identity φ² = φ + 1 for the golden ratio.

mainTheorems.name: vanDoornConstant
mainTheorems.description: The Van Doorn upper-bound constant 2φ^(5/2) ≈ 6.66 on the limsup of the normalized density.

mainTheorems.name: liminfStrictlyGreaterThanOne
mainTheorems.description: Formalizes open question 2: whether the liminf of the normalized density is strictly greater than 1 for every additive complement of squares.

mainTheorems.name: liminf_gt_one_from_bounds
mainTheorems.description: Derives that the liminf of the normalized density exceeds 1 for any additive complement of squares, by combining the 4/π lower bound with 4/π > 1.
mainTheorems.leanType:
(A : Set ℕ)
    (hA : IsAdditiveComplementOfSquares A) :
    (1 : ℝ) < liminf (fun N => normalizedDensity A N) atTop
